newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai 1996 foreign investment seen at 57 bln baht.
newsitem.headline: Thai 1996 foreign investment seen at 57 bln baht.

text.p: Preliminary figures show that the amount of foreign direct investment to Thailand in 1996 reached 57.43 billion baht ($2.2 billion) compared with 49.89 billion in 1995, a Bank of Thailand official said on Friday.
Real estate remained a focus of foreign direct investment (FDI) in 1996 with 18.81 billion baht invested in the sector compared with 21.24 billion baht a year earlier, the official told Reuters.
The sector which attracted the second largest FDI in 1996 was industry, followed by trade and financial institutions respectively.
The United States overtook Japan in 1996 as the biggest foreign direct investor in Thailand and put in 15.89 billion baht in various projects, against 6.47 billion baht in 1995.
ASEAN countries followed with investment worth 12.34 billion baht directly in Thailand last year, a sharp rise from 3.98 billion baht a year earlier.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, Philippines, Vietnam and Brunei.
FDI from Japan, on the other hand, dropped to 9.76 billion baht last year from 13.85 billion baht in 1995.
Foreign direct investment is a form of capital inflow most welcomed by developing countries as it comprises funds which are committed to a specific country for a long term.
Unlike bank loans or any short-term speculative inflows, foreign investors, through FDI, share the country's risks and will reap benefits only if the enterprise turns profitable.
